In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SVM-RFE does not work because it is a recursive method.
SVM-RFE is a good method for feature selection and classification, but it is not the best method for feature selection.
SVM-RFE is not superior to other feature selection methods, and it is the recursive nature of the algorithm that makes it work better in practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SVM-RFE is not the only successful method for recursive feature elimination and that SVM and Rocchio are both effective in RFE.
SVM-RFE is not a panacea for feature selection, and that the choice of a classifier is crucial for RFE.

(i) SVM and RR perform well in recursive settings but not non-recursive settings; (ii) SVM-RFE and RR-RFE perform similarly well; (iii) SVM-RFE is more robust in the choice of the parameter C, while RR-RFE is more sensitive in the choice of lambda; (iv) the success of SVM/Ridge regression comes mainly from the recursive nature of the algorithm rather than the choice of the specific classifier.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recursive process is the key factor that makes SVM-RFE successful.
the success of SVM and RR in RFE comes from the ability of their loss function to penalize the features that are not important.
the choice of the base learner has a significant impact on the performance of RFE.
